title: Text Mining Example
text: cleaning preparing free-text fields, next step natural language processing tasks tokenization. Tokenization process partitioning sentences, paragraphs, documents smaller units individual words (unigrams) contiguous sequences n words (n-grams). smaller units referred tokens provide feature-based representation text. unnest_tokens function tidytext splits column tokens, resulting one-token-per-row dataframe. arguments unnest_tokens include following: output: Name column containing unnested tokens input: Name column containing text split tokens token: Unit tokenizing. default, set “words”, resulting unnesting unigrams. Additional options include ngrams, skip_ngrams, sentences, lines, paragraphs. order unnest ngrams, additional argument n required specify length word sequences(.e. n = 2 bigrams, n = 3 trigrams).
code: cc_unigrams <- data %>%    unnest_tokens(output = word, input = chief_complaint_parsed, token = "words") %>%    filter(!is.na(word)) %>%    anti_join(stop_words)  cc_bigrams <- data %>%    unnest_tokens(output = bigram, input = chief_complaint_parsed,                  token = "ngrams", n = 2) %>%    filter(!is.na(bigram)) %>%    separate(bigram, into = c("word1", "word2"), sep = " ",             remove = FALSE) %>%    filter(!word1 %in% stop_words) %>%   filter(!word2 %in% stop_words)  cc_trigrams <- data %>%    unnest_tokens(output = trigram, input = chief_complaint_parsed,                  token = "ngrams", n = 3) %>%    separate(trigram, into = c("word1", "word2", "word3"), sep = " ", remove = FALSE) %>%    filter(!word1 %in% stop_words) %>%    filter(!word2 %in% stop_words) %>%    filter(!word3 %in% stop_words)
